task: SQLite Contention at Scale + DB Partitioning

db_partition.py.description: Partitioned SQLite database manager splitting monolithic DB into 4 functional partitions
key_features: Unified PartitionedStore interface routing to correct DB by table name
Per-partition WAL mode, busy_timeout=30s, BEGIN IMMEDIATE
Thread-local connection pooling (1 conn per DB per thread)
Retry on SQLITE_BUSY: 5 retries, exponential backoff + jitter
Migration helper: migrate_from_monolithic() for incremental adoption

contention_monitor.py.description: Real-time contention monitoring with alerting, JSONL logging, and stress testing
key_features: Per-partition metrics: ops/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, SQLITE_BUSY rate, WAL size
Configurable alert thresholds with critical/warning levels
JSONL log output for time-series analysis
Background daemon thread mode with configurable interval
Self-test: concurrent writer stress simulation (N writers, configurable duration)
Probe writes to measure actual write latency

partitioning_design.rationale: Split tables by who writes to them and how often, keeping each partition under SOP-034's 4-writer limit

hub.db.rationale: Agent registry and instructions are coordinator-mediated. Only the coordinator writes instructions; agents write their own status row.

queue.db.contention_risk: Low - atomic steal with BEGIN IMMEDIATE prevents double-claim
queue.db.rationale: Work queue operations are naturally serialized by steal semantics. Pipeline stage transitions are infrequent.

comms.db.contention_risk: Low - each team updates its own presence/progress row
comms.db.rationale: Channel and presence writes are partitioned by team. Message writes go to team-specific bus files (JSONL), not DB.

findings.db.contention_risk: Low - mostly INSERTs, rare UPDATE conflicts
findings.db.rationale: Findings, scratchpad, and help protocol are append-heavy. Conflicts only arise on help_request acceptance (handled by BEGIN IMMEDIATE).

backwards_compatibility.existing_code_impact: Zero - existing modules continue using single DB path
migration_path: 2. Run migrate_from_monolithic() to copy data to partitioned DBs
3. New code uses PartitionedStore; old code unchanged
4. Gradually migrate old modules to PartitionedStore
5. Retire monolithic DB once all modules migrated
